publications.title: Finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions
publications.summary: Today, the Reserve Bank released the second edition of its biennial Report titled " Finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions ". The theme of this edition is ‘Local Finances and Capacity Building in Rural India'. Drawing upon a balanced panel of 2.25 lakh Gram Panchayats for the period 2022-23 to 2024-25, the Report presents an assessment of their finances and their role in achieving sustainable and inclusive rural socio-economic development. Highlights: Gram Panchayat finances strengthened during 2022-23 and 2023-24; they, however, remain dependent on intergovernmental transfers, accounting for about 90 per cent of total receipts, while own source revenues (OSR) accounted for a modest share of about 10 per cent, predominantly driven by non-tax receipts such as interest receipts, Panchayati Raj programme funds and user charges. publications.title: Geordie Shore star and illegal finfluencer sentenced for promoting high-risk investments on social media
publications.summary: Aaron Chalmers, a reality TV star and social media content creator, and finfluencer Jason Agbodza have been sentenced for illegally promoting an unauthorised foreign exchange trading scheme on social media. Chalmers, 39 and from Newcastle, was sentenced at City of London Magistrates Court. He previously pleaded guilty and today (19 November) was fined £3,072 and ordered to pay costs of £2,836.Having risen to fame on Geordie Shore, Chalmers has more than 2 million followers on Instagram. Agbodza, 35, of London, was also fined £1,173 and ordered to pay costs of £2,114 after pleading guilty.Both men encouraged followers to invest in foreign exchange (forex or FX) trading through contracts for difference (CFDs), without being authorised to promote them. publications.title: FINMA publishes guidance to optimise the supervision of portfolio managers and trustees
publications.summary: In new guidance, the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority FINMA sets out measures designed to optimise the implementation of the two-tier supervisory system for portfolio managers and trustees, as far as the law allows. It is simplifying procedures for changes to licences, structuring fees in a way that is more in line with the principle of causation, and advocating for an even more risk-based supervisory approach.

publications.title: UK financial watchdogs clarify cyber expectations as attacks rise
publications.summary: UK’s financial regulators are proposing new guidance to help financial services firms prepare for and recover from cyber incidents as threats grow. The Bank of England’s most recent Systemic Risk Survey cited cyber as one of the risks that would have the greatest impact on the UK financial system. October 2026 saw the second-highest monthly number of cyber incidents reported to the FCA in 5 years, and the highest in the past 18 months, 52% above the previous high recorded in May 2025.In response, the Bank, FCA and Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) are bringing together existing requirements and lessons from supervisory experience to give firms greater clarity about what is expected of them.The proposed guidance aligns with recognised cyber frameworks, including the National Cyber Security Centre’s (NCSC) Cyber Assessment Framework. publications.title: DRSP supervisory responsibilities remain unchanged following ESMA assessment
publications.summary: DRSP supervisory responsibilities remain unchanged following ESMA assessment 18 November 2026 Market data Supervision The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has finalised its annual assessment of the derogation criteria for Data Reporting Services Providers (DRSPs) . ESMA’s supervisory responsibilities for DRSPs will remain unchanged, as the ten DRSPs currently supervised by ESMA continue to exceed the relevant derogation thresholds, while the derogated DRSPs remain under the supervision of their respective national competent authorities (NCAs). The assessment is based on data from the 2025 calendar year. Next steps Following the notification of the outcome of the assessment, ESMA will continue to monitor developments and engage with NCAs and supervised entities to ensure a smooth and transparent supervisory process.
